title: Commercial Mortgages UK
summary: The /commercial-mortgages/ page was not retrievable directly; search (a) could not fetch it, search (b) indexed it under the title 'Commercial Mortgages UK' and summarised its content, search (c) returned nothing about Silver Oak. What the results state about the page: it addresses two audiences, owner-occupiers (business owners buying the premises they trade from, gaining security of tenure, avoiding rent reviews and building a tangible balance-sheet asset) and property investors (buying commercial property to let to third-party tenants, often seeking finance that maximises leverage to amplify Return on Equity), and it states that LTVs for commercial mortgages are usually between 65% and 75% depending on the property and circumstances. Related site pages add: an 8-12 week application-to-completion timescale and a cost list (lender arrangement fee, valuation fee, legal fee, broker fee) from the FAQ; sectors covered (retail, office, logistics, care homes, student accommodation, hotels) from the home page; and conflicting loan-size (over GBP 500,000 vs GBP 2-20m) and lender-count (300 / 700+ / 800+) claims across pages. H1, meta description, rates, fees specific to this page, process steps and CTAs were not revealed.

sections.heading: Owner-occupiers
sections.content: [b] (search-tool summary of the page) Owner-occupiers are described as business owners buying the premises they trade from. Owning the premises gives them security of tenure, avoids rent reviews, and builds a tangible asset on the company balance sheet. [seed] The site navigation labels this segment 'Commercial Mortgages (Owner-Occupiers regulated, Investors)', i.e. owner-occupier commercial mortgages are flagged as regulated.

sections.heading: Property investors
sections.content: [b] (search-tool summary of the page) Property investors are described as buyers who purchase commercial property specifically to let out to third-party tenants. The page says investors often seek commercial finance that maximises leverage to amplify their Return on Equity (ROE).

sections.heading: Loan to value
sections.content: [b] (search-tool summary of the page) LTVs for commercial mortgages are usually between 65% and 75% depending on the property and circumstances.

sections.heading: Core uses and positioning (attribution uncertain: 'its commercial page')
sections.content: [a] The search-tool summary says 'its commercial page lists borrowing, developing, refinancing and acquiring as core uses, and states that it aims for speed and transparency', and that the firm 'positions itself as an independent commercial mortgage broker for UK commercial real estate'. The summary does not say whether 'its commercial page' means /commercial-mortgages/ or /commercial-mortgage-broker/ (the latter is the URL actually listed in result (a)).

sections.heading: Costs and timescales (FAQ page, not this page)
sections.content: [a] The FAQ says fees are set out at the outset, and lists common costs as the lender arrangement fee, valuation fee, legal fee and broker fee. [b] The FAQ adds that a commercial mortgage application typically takes 8 to 12 weeks from application to completion.

sections.heading: Loan size and lender network (contradictions across sources)
sections.content: [a] A third-party directory describes the firm as 'specializing in large loans of £2-£20m'; the firm's own homepage instead says it works on loans over £500,000. [a] Lender count varies: older listings mention 300 lenders, the commercial mortgage broker page cites 700+, the homepage and a 2026 award listing cite 800+. [seed] /about-us/ says 'has focused on loans between £500K to £20m'; /commercial-mortgage-broker/ says 'the firm also focuses on larger loan sizes of £2-£20 million which sets us apart from the majority of the commercial bridging loan market'.
